claim: P1 engineering non-inferiority of the finite batch-structured consumer route against Marl and oneTBB under one frozen semantic and four-worker physical-core contract

configuration.delivery_shape: source-built static library in a separate peer process
configuration.route: Marl Scheduler::enqueue plus one caller-owned WaitGroup per finite batch
configuration.worker_topology: four dedicated pinned Marl workers; the external process role only submits the root and waits

configuration.delivery_shape: source-built oneTBB runtime in a separate peer process
configuration.route: task_arena(max_concurrency=4) plus parallel_for with unit grain and simple_partitioner
configuration.worker_topology: four pinned arena slots; the external process role enqueues the root and waits without entering the arena

ownership_topology.candidate: One admitted HYLE root Fiber calls bulk_execute for each batch; at most four raw runners claim unit indices, write caller-owned slots and share one batch completion/error/cancel state
ownership_topology.peer: One admitted Marl root task enqueues one Task per unit index, writes the same caller-owned slots and waits on one Marl WaitGroup per batch
ownership_topology.equivalence: Both run 16 batches of 128 non-suspending 1024-element tiles on four pinned workers; setup/root admission are excluded, all bodies succeed, cancellation is dormant, the external role never computes a tile, and each batch is quiescent before result consumption

material_contribution.derivation: Current Graph range work and llama.cpp/ggml finite graph episodes require batch-level completion with caller-owned results rather than one independently owned future per work item

workloads.semantic_contract: Execute every indexed non-suspending tile exactly once, write every caller-owned result slot and synchronously quiesce each finite batch without per-item result/control ownership

input.distribution: fixed deterministic 1024-element uint64 tile with one seed per indexed item

workloads.setup: Provider construction, worker pinning, input/result allocation, expected checksum, root admission and one complete warmup batch are outside measurement
charged_phases: 1024-element deterministic tile for every indexed item
whole-batch completion and exact result consumption
